items.title: Reggie Watkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, May 22, 2018
items.q: going with Maynard in 1999, by a year later I was musical director.

ctx.x: I’d have older guys show them to me. Because when we came onto the ship, I remember the first ship I came onto in a quartet, the other band was guys that, they knew a million tunes. And they were thirty, forty years older than us. So they would be a resource. They might have — I remember that guy having a stack of real books but we didn’t have that. He had a stack of real books. So that was one resource. But also you could just catch them after their set, because I would figure things out and say, “Hey what’s the…

an amazing drummer. So I’m getting just all this experience there. And then Maynard Ferguson would always have young guys in the band. And where they were from, it kind of moved like a wave. So if you had a lot of guys — if there were guys in the band from North Texas then they would recommend their buddies from North Texas. So there were some guys that got on to the band from Pittsburgh. And that began a wave, and then I got recommended onto the band and I subsequently recommended other people onto the band. So…
Because you had the income, you had the gig and you had the travel.
